ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=-\frac{3}{4}x^{2}+bx+c$ intersects the x-axis at point $A(4,0)$ and the y-axis at point $B(0,3)$. Point $M(m,0)$ is a moving point on line segment $OA$, and the line passing through point $M$ and perpendicular to the x-axis intersects line $AB$ and the parabola at points $P$ and $N$, respectively. If the quadrilateral formed by points $P$, $N$, $B$, and $O$ is a parallelogram, find the value of $m$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the equation of line AB be $y=px+q$,\\
Substituting A(4, 0) and B(0, 3) gives $\left\{\begin{array}{l}4p+q=0 \\ q=3\end{array}\right.$,\\
Solving for $p$ and $q$ yields $\left\{\begin{array}{l}p=-\frac{3}{4} \\ q=3\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ The equation of line AB is $y=-\frac{3}{4}x+3$,\\
$\because$ M(m, 0), and MN$\perp$x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ N(m, $-\frac{3}{4}m^{2}+\frac{9}{4}m+3$), and P(m, $-\frac{3}{4}m+3$),\\
$\therefore$ NP= $-\frac{3}{4}m^{2}+3m$, OB=3,\\
$\because$ NP$\parallel$OB, and the quadrilateral formed by vertices P, N, B, and O is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ NP= OB, i.e., $-\frac{3}{4}m^{2}+3m=3$,\\
Upon rearrangement: $m^{2}-4m+4=0$,\\
Solving yields: $m=\boxed{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is near the origin, A is marked on the positive half-axis of the x-axis, and B is marked on the positive half-axis of the y-axis; a downward-opening parabola passes near B and intersects the x-axis at A; line AB passes from B downward to the right through A. The figure mainly shows A, B, O, as well as the parabola and line AB; the positions of M, P, N are defined by the text of the problem. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem and the diagram, read A=(4,0), B=(0,3), O=(0,0), M=(m,0), and the line passing through M and perpendicular to the x-axis is x=m. The parabola is y=-3/4 x^2+bx+c. Because B(0,3) is on the parabola, c=3. Because A(4,0) is on the parabola, -3/4·16+4b+3=0, that is, -12+4b+3=0, obtaining 4b=9, so b=9/4. Therefore the parabola is y=-3/4 x^2+9/4 x+3. Line AB passes through A(4,0) and B(0,3), and the slope is (0-3)/(4-0)=-3/4, so the equation of line AB is y=-3/4 x+3. The vertical line x=m intersects line AB at P, so P=(m,-3/4 m+3). The vertical line x=m intersects the parabola at N, so N=(m,-3/4 m^2+9/4 m+3). Therefore the length of PN is N_y-P_y=(-3/4 m^2+9/4 m+3)-(-3/4 m+3)=-3/4 m^2+3m. Also OB=3. If P, N, B, O form a parallelogram, and PN and OB are both vertical opposite sides, then PN=OB=3 is required, so -3/4 m^2+3m=3. Rearranging gives -3m^2+12m=12, that is, m^2-4m+4=0, that is, (m-2)^2=0. Therefore m=2.
